source_review.notes: Checked current OASIS Virtio 1.4, Linux Virtio and KVM, and QEMU device, vhost-user, memory, security and migration documentation. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; normative requirements, implementation APIs, backend protocols, abstract models and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked capacity, available, used, reclaimed, descriptor, length, per-request work, notification, transition, batch and feature-set notation.
Reviewed queue-order inequalities, wrapped slots, checked chain length, amortized batch cost and negotiated feature intersection.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates logical queue progress from physical slots, granted buffer extent from raw fields and offered features from active semantics.

evidence: Executed publication, two device batches, reclamation and physical-slot wrap in a four-entry toy queue.
Confirmed publish slots 0,1,2,3,0,1; ordered batches; final progress 6/6/6 and four free descriptors; independently recomputed amortized costs 13.8, 3.3 and 2.175 microseconds.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates counter and ownership arithmetic only; it implements no Virtio layout, barrier, descriptor validation, DMA, notification or backend.

evidence: Re-derived valid queue state from reclaimed-through-used-through-available ordering and capacity-bounded unreclaimed work.
Checked descriptor-length summation, fixed-cost amortization by batch and active features as accepted offered features with dependencies.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are queue reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of Virtio 1.4, a transport, device type, memory model or migration protocol.

evidence: Reviewed cyclic and indirect chains, index and address wrap, short writable buffers, stale descriptors, feature mismatch and notification races.
Reviewed reset with late completion, IOTLB removal, confidential memory, backend crash, block persistence, network offloads, multiqueue order and migration.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Feature, queue, ordering, validation, address, reset, backend, device-specific, hotplug and migration boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced a chain from driver construction through ordered publication, backend validation, device access, ordered completion and reclamation.
Verified negotiated-only semantics, bounded occupancy, directional grants, no lost wakeups, one completion and generation-fenced reset.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats common Virtio state, transport, queues, device commands, backend work and lifecycle as one contract with explicit ownership transfer.

evidence: Reviewed queue safety and liveness across driver, device, notification, reset and migration transitions.
Constructed counterexamples for offered-as-active, descriptor-as-address, interrupt-as-memory-barrier, kick-as-request, vhost-as-userspace-free and migrated-indices-as-migrated-device.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable virtual-device obligations, not a formal proof of Virtio, Linux, QEMU, a backend, device, driver, transport or hardware implementation.

evidence: Audited uses of offered, selected, negotiated, published, available, used, reclaimed, completed, reset, drained and migrated.
Confirmed normative contracts, implementation behavior, abstract formulas, operational guidance, examples and assurance limits remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Offered is not labeled negotiated, an index is not labeled ownership without ordering, block completion is not labeled stable media and transparent migration is not labeled driver renegotiation.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-085/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the wrap-safe queue toy.
Reviewed required specification, transport, features, queue format, backend, VMM, kernel, IOMMU, memory mapping, interrupt, reset and migration evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one abstract queue sequence only; it provides no evidence for memory ordering, DMA safety, backend isolation, device correctness, durability, liveness or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed Virtio as a negotiated shared-memory ownership-transfer protocol whose device, transport, queue and backend semantics must remain coherent.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including status, features, split and packed rings, descriptor validation, barriers, notifications, reset, vhost, vhost-user, vDPA, IOTLBs, block/network semantics and migration. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from virtual device contracts and negotiation through queue layouts, ownership, ordering, notifications, reset, backend placement, device semantics and migration, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, OASIS Virtio editor, kernel or VMM maintainer, device-backend engineer, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
